tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.1 on Sep 1, bringing it to Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards for keeping data in a controlled cloud environment.
whats_new: AINews' Sep 2 recap confirms the launch pairs a new SOTA model with a 75% cache price cut and 70% more output tokens.
why_it_matters: Fable 5.1 is available on Bedrock from day one, so teams already standardized on AWS can adopt it without a separate procurement path — and the pricing change changes the cost math for anyone benchmarking it against the prior generation.

status.detail: Claude Fable 5.1 shipped Sep 1 with AWS Bedrock availability and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards; Simon Willison's hands-on the same day praises its coding, knowledge-work, and long-running task performance; Sep 2 coverage adds the pricing details.

beats.headline: Claude Fable 5.1 launches on Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS
beats.summary: Anthropic's post covers Fable 5.1's improvements and the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards for keeping data in a controlled cloud environment.

beats.headline: Simon Willison's hands-on: Fable 5.1 "sets a new standard for coding, knowledge work, and long-running problem-solving"
Pricing details confirmed: 75% cache price cut, 70% more output tokens

open_questions: Does the 75% cache-price cut and output-token increase apply uniformly across the Bedrock, Claude Platform, and direct-API channels?
How does Fable 5.1's long-running-task performance hold up on multi-hour agentic workloads beyond Willison's initial hands-on?
take_for_builders: If you're already on Bedrock, evaluate Fable 5.1 against your current Claude model on both the new pricing and long-running-task performance before migrating production traffic.
